newsitem.title: LATVIA: Key Latvian confectionary firm gets bourse quote.
newsitem.headline: Key Latvian confectionary firm gets bourse quote.

text.p: One of the largest confectionary firms in the Baltic state of Latvia, Staburadze, is to start stock exchange trade on December 10, the bourse said on Tuesday.
The company had turnover in the first 10 months of 1996 of 5.8 million lats and it made a profit of 256,685 lats, stock exchange president Uldis Cerps told a news conference.
"This is positive news," Cerps said, announcing the start of trade in Staburadze, a house-hold name in Latvia.
It sells around 90 percent of its produce in Latvia and the rest goes to the other Baltic states plus C.I.S. countries.
The company's share capital consists of 1.9 million shares, of which some 59.64 percent is owned by small shareholders while the company's workers have 20 percent.
The shares will start trade with a value of one lat.
Latvijas Krajbanka, currently state-owned but included in the privatisation list for early next year, holds 15 percent.
The company employs some 498 people and has to maintain these staffing levels for the coming three years.
